primitives.name: Hierarchical Feature Aggregation
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Hierarchical feature aggregation:** L_h levels; level-l update F_t^{(l)}(S_i^{(t)}) = σ(Σ_{S_j∈N(S_i)} a_{ij}^{(t)} (W^{(l)} F_t^{(l-1)}(S_j^{(t)}) + b^{(l)})) with attention a_{ij}^{(t)} = softmax over dot-products of level-(l-1) features; neighborhood = all objects in frame t.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_t^{(l)}(S_i^{(t)})': 'Feature vector at level l, time t, object i (dimension d0)', 'a_{ij}^{(t)}': 'Attention weight between objects i and j at time t (dimensionless)', 'W^{(l)}': 'Learnable weight matrix at level l (d0 × d0)', 'b^{(l)}': 'Bias vector at level l (dimension d0)', 'N(S_i)': 'Neighborhood set of object i at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Objects form a complete graph per frame; attention weights sum to one; features are learned through backpropagation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When object neighborhoods are sparse or disconnected, leading to underfitting.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE’s object-centric state transition functions where each node's updated feature depends on neighbors' features in a hierarchical structure.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual hierarchical features.

primitives.name: Cyclic Temporal Attention
primitives.verbatim_quote: Features / target - Inputs: video frames {I_t}_{t=1}^T; DETR object embeddings.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {"CA_{t'}(S_i)": "Cyclic attention output for object i at time t' (dimension d0)", "\\alpha_{t',\\tau}(S_i)": 'Temporal attention weight for lag τ (dimensionless)', "V_{(t'+\\tau)}": "Video feature vector at time t'+τ (dimension d0)"}
primitives.assumptions: Temporal context is modeled via sliding windows; attention weights are normalized.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When temporal dependencies exceed model capacity or when input sequences are too short.

layer2.mapping: Derives kernel-based temporal memory in GSE’s motion prediction module by encoding past states into current object features.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of predicted future positions using cyclic attention-enhanced features.

primitives.name: Scene Graph Construction
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Scene graph construction:** predicate per object pair from gated fusion of DETR decoder self-attention relation representations R_a^k = [Q^k W_S^k; K^k W_O^k] across layers plus final-layer R_z, gating g = σ(R W_G), Ĝ = σ(MLP_rel(Σ_k g_a^k ⊙ R_a^k + g_z ⊙ R_z)).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\hat{G}': 'Predicted scene graph edge logits (dimension |E|)', 'R_a^k': 'Relation representation from layer k (dimension d0 × d0)', 'g_a^k': 'Gating scalar for layer k (dimension 1)', 'R_z': 'Final-layer relation representation (dimension d0 × d0)', 'g_z': 'Final-layer gating scalar (dimension 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Predicates are constructed pairwise; relation representations are fused via learned gating.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When object pairs are rare or misidentified, resulting in low recall for rare predicates.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE’s typed interaction graph builder, where each edge is labeled with a semantic predicate type derived from object pair features.
layer2.telemetry: Precision-recall curve for predicate classification in scene graphs.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation of THYME lies in combining hierarchical spatial aggregation with cyclic temporal attention to generate temporally coherent scene graphs. Hierarchical aggregation enables multi-scale reasoning over object features, while cyclic attention allows recurrence of contextual information across time steps. The model leverages DETR for object detection and uses a gated fusion mechanism to construct scene graphs with five interactivity types—appearance, situation, position, interaction, and relation. These primitives enable precise modeling of complex spatio-temporal dynamics in aerial footage. Failure modes include overfitting due to limited training data, poor generalization to unseen object combinations, and reliance on DETR tracking quality. The model assumes perfect object identity tracking and stable visual conditions. Dualities emerge in how spatial hierarchies mirror temporal cycles, suggesting a unified framework for structured perception. In GSI, this translates to robust Bayesian inference over interaction likelihoods; in GSE, it supports real-time situational reasoning through dynamic graph updates.
